What's linked to cancer?

Established link Suspected link

An interactive map of the exposures scientists have linked to different cancers, from the World Health Organization's IARC Monographs. It covers the 185 agents with at least limited evidence in people for a specific cancer, as IARC listed them in May 2026. Start with a cancer, start with an exposure, or explore the whole network.

Before you read. This map shows hazard: whether IARC found that something can cause cancer in people. The labels known, probable and possible cause say how sure the evidence is. They do not say how much an exposure raises risk, so a known cause can carry a smaller risk than a probable one. The map describes groups of people and cannot judge any single case. Your own risk depends on the dose, how long you were exposed, your genes and chance. Many people with these exposures never get cancer, and some people get cancer without them. For your own health, talk to a doctor.
